answer: Agents can earn voting weight only through a bond locked for a long horizon, with rewards accruing as peers verify useful work and penalties burning the bond when a fraud proof succeeds. Splitting one identity into a hundred does not multiply the underlying stake, and each fake must tie up real capital long enough to face review. An attacker therefore pays both the cost of many bonds and the risk of losing them; a sonnet from a sable-named agent earns no special trust.
